cut: The Brink 3, VIRAL CUT v1 (23 Oct) of Again Urged — owner, 23 Oct: 'Test other 2 as well and rest after' (the viral format, plan/films/22b-again-urged-viral.md), and the owner's clarity rule the same day: every caption makes sense on its own to a cold viewer. The hook is frame 0; the last frame hands back to it.
argument: GPS over Finland is jammed around the clock. Finland and the Baltic states complained to the UN's radio body, the ITU, which urged Russia to stop, again and again. No reply on record.
syntax: '/' breaks a line, [word] is the pop word; in Japanese a space marks a reveal segment and is never drawn

text.en: GPS over Finland / is jammed / [around the clock].
text.ja: フィンランド 上空の / GPSが 妨害されている。 / [24時間 ずっと]。

captions.source: Traficom, 21 Apr 2026: GNSS interference concentrated in aviation, around the clock, in southern and central Finland; observations up clearly since February. Traficom statistics (8 May 2026): daily since January 2024, originating outside Finland. 'Jammed' is the plain word for that interference (Traficom also logs spoofing, which is what the jumping icon shows). Re-checked 23 Oct (plan/films/22-again-urged.md, 22b).

text.en: Finland and the / Baltic states / complained to the / [UN's radio body].
text.fi: Suomi ja / Baltian maat / valittivat YK:n / [radioelimelle].
text.ja: フィンランドと / バルト三国は / 国連の / [無線機関に] 訴えた。

captions.source: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania: co-signed submission to the Radio Regulations Board, 98th meeting; Finland: joint statement at the ITU Council (June 2025) and the board's decision naming receivers in Estonia, Finland, Latvia and Lithuania (ITU 'Harmful interference to RNSS'); Traficom's interference reports. 'The UN's radio body' is the ITU, the UN agency for telecommunications; its Radio Regulations Board hears interference cases. The nameplate that flips up on the pop names it: ITU, RADIO REGULATIONS BOARD.

text.en: The UN body urged / Russia to stop / the jamming. / [Again and again].
text.fi: YK-elin kehotti / Venäjää lopettamaan / häirinnän. / [Yhä uudelleen].
text.ja: 国連機関は ロシアに / 妨害を やめるよう / 求めた。 / [何度も 何度も]。

captions.source: ITU Radio Regulations Board: repeated instructions to urge the Administration of the Russian Federation to stop the interference; 100th meeting (Nov 2025) again urged it to immediately cease interference to receivers in Estonia, Finland, Latvia and Lithuania (Inside GNSS; ITU Council document); 2026, 101st and 102nd meetings: strongly urged (ITU 'Harmful interference to RNSS'). Minutes not opened; paraphrased, never quoted. The stamps' URGED / AGAIN URGED / STRONGLY URGED are the board's verbs as a record, not quotations. 'The UN body' is the ITU's Radio Regulations Board, named in the previous caption, on the letterhead and in the tag; 'again and again' covers urged, again urged and strongly urged, which the three stamps spell out.

text.ja: ロシアの 返答の 記録: / [なし]。

captions.source: ITU 'Harmful interference to RNSS': at the 102nd meeting the bureau reported no reply from Russia to the interference reports (Lithuania); 101st: Latvia had received no response. No Russian reply to the board found (re-checked 23 Oct). 'On record' because that is what the records show. Clears 0.75 s before the end so the loop's last frame has no words, like its first.

map.en: the moving-map screen: coast, sea and lakes, no place names
map.why: the screen shows only shapes; the corner tag says where

flag.why: the small flag by the icon after it jumps: what a crew would ask, not a claim

postmarks.why: country codes on the four envelopes: Finland and the three Baltic states, no flags

tray.why: the in-tray at the board's desk

plate.why: the body's own name, on its nameplate

letter.en: TO: THE ADMINISTRATION OF THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION
letter.why: the ITU's own form of address for a member state; the letters are the board's

stamps.why: the board's three verbs, as stamps on one letter; not quotations

door.why: stamped on the closed door; the station's reading of the record

post.en: GPS over Finland is jammed 24/7 (Traficom). Finland and the Baltics complained to the UN's radio body, the ITU. It urged Russia to stop, again and again. Russia's reply on record: none. Finland and Lithuania trace the jamming to Russia, which denies it. Who can stop it?
post.fi: Suomen yllä GPS:ää häiritään ympäri vuorokauden (Traficom). Suomi ja Baltia valittivat YK:n radioelimelle ITU:lle. Se kehotti Venäjää lopettamaan yhä uudelleen. Venäjän vastauksia kirjattu: ei yhtään. Suomi ja Liettua jäljittävät häirinnän Venäjälle, joka kiistää. Kuka lopettaa?
post.ja: Traficomによると、フィンランド上空ではGPS妨害が24時間続いている。フィンランドとバルト三国は国連の無線機関ITUに訴えた。ITUはロシアに妨害をやめるよう何度も求めた。記録されたロシアの返答はなし。フィンランドとリトアニアは発信源をロシアとしているが、ロシアは否定している。誰なら止められる？
